title: Metal-Organic Frameworks, Chemistry's New Miracle Materials (2018)
summary: UC Berkeley chemistry researchers discuss Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), highly porous materials made from metal clusters connected by organic linkers, with potential applications in gas storage, separation, and catalysis. The article highlights Berkeley labs developing novel MOFs with extremely high surface areas and tunable properties for clean energy and environmental applications.
problem_solved: Creating ultra-porous materials with customizable structures for efficient gas storage, separation, and chemical reactions
why_valuable: MOFs offer record-breaking surface areas and precise structural control, enabling breakthroughs in clean energy storage, carbon capture, and selective separations that traditional materials cannot achieve
